title: Frostline Energy - Implementation ignition & network play
summary: Kickoff for Frostline Energy onboarding: reviewed integration pattern (private VPC deployment vs dedicated), security requirements (KMS, audit logs, SOC2), initial performance goals and pilot scope. Agreed next steps: provide security packet, run a 48h throughput/latency benchmark, and schedule SE-led POC next Tues.
next_steps: Redwood to share security packet (SOC2/ISO docs, audit log sample) by 2026-12-28
SE to provision benchmark harness and test plan by 2026-12-29
Customer to provide sample traffic profile and 3 production prompts by 2027-01-04
Schedule POC kickoff (2h deep-dive) for 2026-12-29 10:00 PT
action_items: Lena Park - share security packet and SSO requirements - due 2026-12-28
Diego Ramos - create benchmark harness and run 48h throughput test on Dedicated config - due 2026-12-29
Priya Menon - send sample prompt set and traffic distribution - due 2027-01-04
Kaitlyn Cho - confirm KMS provider and compliance checklist - due 2027-01-05
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-23 07:00 PT / Duration 62 min / Attendees listed above

[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone thanks for making time today um this is Lena from Redwood inference, i'll kick off real quick --- agenda is alignment on the onboarding path, network layout (VPC/private), security, and a short run-of-show for the pilot.
[00:25] Tomás Alvarez: hey Lena, thanks. we are mostly interested in private deployment options cause of data residency and latency. quick note, our infra team prefers keystore via our in-house HSM.
[00:38] Marcus Liu: great, Marcus here, i'll be your CSM. just to set expectations — we typically do a 48 hour bench then a 2 week pilot for productioning.
[00:48] Priya Menon: quick question — do you support pinning model variants? we need deterministic output for a subset of prompts for audit.
[00:57] Diego Ramos: yes, you can pin model versions and we have rollout policies (canary/A-B/auto-fallback). there was a hiccup with older docs where we called it "model snapshotting" but it's really version pinning.
[01:10] Priya Menon: ok good. also latency SLOs — our SLAs are 95th <120ms for short responses, is that realistic?
[01:20] Diego Ramos: depends on config; hosted small-provision we might not hit that consistently, Dedicated with optimized kernels + KV cache should be doable for <120ms on avg for short sequences. but if you need strict SLOs, we recommend Dedicated or Private with reserved GPU pool.
[01:37] Priya Menon: and cost delta? feels like a big jump.
[01:41] Lena Park: yes that's the normal trade — dedicated/private gives predictability and lower p99s but commit costs higher; we can show cost per token projections once we have your traffic shape.
[01:52] Tomás Alvarez: about network — we run everything in our AWS account, want Redwood private control plane but egress rules locked down. can you do VPC peering or transit gateway?
[02:03] Diego Ramos: yep we support both peering and TGW, also can do on-prem package if you need air-gapped. note: on the peering setup we usually need a small reverse-proxy in your VPC to handshake with the control plane, docs will show IP ranges etc.
[02:20] Kaitlyn Cho: from compliance, we need audit logs retention 1 year, SAML SSO, and KMS integration with our existing HSM; do you rotate keys automatically?
[02:31] Lena Park: short answer yes; we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS & customer-managed HSM) and can support bring-your-own-keys. audit logs and retention settings configurable via Console, we'll include examples.
[02:44] Ravi Kapoor: one tricky bit — our traffic includes lots of long context chains (support transcripts ~2.5k tokens) and we want to know about KV cache behavior and cost impacts.
[02:55] Diego Ramos: the runtime uses prefix/KV caching to reduce tokenization cost; for long contexts you may see higher memory usage, we'll propose quantized weights to save GPU mem. sometimes the transcript got transcribed as "KV cash" in older notes, so just flagging the oddities in speech-to-text.
[03:12] Priya Menon: hah yeah saw that in the doc. ok bench specifics — can you simulate our bursty diurnal pattern?
[03:19] Marcus Liu: absolutely, Diego will produce a harness. the plan we propose: 48h run with production-sampled traffic (you provide sample), two configs (Dedicated reserved pool vs Private VPC), measure throughput, median and p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:36] Tomás Alvarez: and on the data plane — are logs/evals ever sent to Redwood? or you have option to keep everything customer-side?
[03:44] Diego Ramos: by default logs for observability are stored in the control plane but we have an option to forward logs to your S3 or to keep retention only on customer side for Private deployments. we'll show the controls.
[03:58] Priya Menon: how do rollbacks happen if model quality regresses after a deploy?
[04:05] Diego Ramos: Console supports canary and schema-based regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets; if regressions are detected we can auto-fallback to pin to previous version and alert the team.
[04:17] Maya Bennett: stakeholder question — who's the primary contact for infra cutover?
[04:21] Marcus Liu: Marcus (CSM) will own the project plan; Diego will own the technical runbook; Lena coordinates legal/commercial.
[04:30] Tomás Alvarez: small nit — our infra team requires egress IP allowlist, can you provide static IP ranges?
[04:36] Lena Park: yes we'll share the IP ranges — action item.
[04:40] [noise / cross-talk 04:40-04:55] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[04:56] Priya Menon: ok security docs — can you share SOC2, ISO attestation, penetration test summary and a sanitized audit log example?
[05:06] Lena Park: yes we'll bundle that in the security packet.
[05:09] Kaitlyn Cho: and please include compliance contacts for legal team.
[05:14] Lena Park: will do.
[05:16] Diego Ramos: timeline wise for bench — i'll need your sample prompts and traffic dist by 2027-01-04 to run the planned tests before end of Jan; otherwise we can do a minimal bench with synthetic load earlier.
[05:29] Priya Menon: we can send an initial subset this week but full set maybe Jan 4.
[05:33] Marcus Liu: scheduling POC kickoff — we proposed 2026-12-29 10am PT, does that work?
[05:39] Tomás Alvarez: yes works for us.
[05:42] [06:00] Recap: Lena Park: ok recap — action items: Lena send security packet + IP ranges; Diego build bench + test plan; Priya send prompts and traffic; Kaitlyn validate KMS & compliance checklist. POC kickoff 12/29 10am PT. we'll follow up via email with calendar invite and a short runbook.
[06:20] Priya Menon: thanks everyone excited to get started.
[06:25] Lena Park: thanks all, we'll send docs shortly.
[06:30] End of meeting.
